mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS over three consecutive months signals a monetary easing cycle, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth) signals strengthening demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity prices over the subsequent quarter (60 trading days).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds previous quarter by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically lower than zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend for three consecutive months signals weakening economic activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous year's same month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically lower than zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average, coupled with a concurrent drop in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST), signals a collapse in consumer and housing demand that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall below their 6-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not statistically negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its trend for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in INDPRO and a decrease in UNRATE signals a supply-side expansion with softening labor market pressure, which boosts profit margins and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during a recovery phase following a prior recession.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises while UNRATE falls in the same month, within 12 months of a NBER-defined recession trough
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered post-recession months.
